steps.title: Set up Google Cloud account and verify identity
steps.detail: Sign in to Google Cloud Console, ensure your Google account has 2FA enabled, verify your identity and domain ownership as required for sensitive Gmail scopes (claims f15,f17,f18,f19).

steps.title: Register OAuth client in Google Cloud Console
steps.detail: In Cloud Console go to API & Services → Credentials, create an OAuth client (type Web application). Fill in the app name, authorized redirect URI (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) exactly as documented (claims k3,f12).

steps.title: Configure OAuth consent screen and scopes
steps.detail: Use the OAuth consent screen builder to set app name, support email, logo, and add required Gmail scopes (gmail.readonly,gmail.send,gmail.compose). Submit for verification if scopes are sensitive/restricted (claims f15,f20).

steps.title: Add client credentials to Composio Gmail toolkit
steps.detail: In Composio console, navigate to the Gmail toolkit settings, disable managed auth, paste the client ID and client secret from Google, and set the redirect URI to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (claims k2,k3).

steps.title: Test OAuth flow with internal users
steps.detail: Create test user accounts, initiate Gmail connection through Composio, ensure the consent screen appears, tokens are received, and email actions work. Note that existing users will need to reconnect (claim f4).

steps.title: Submit app for Google verification and Marketplace listing
steps.detail: In Google Cloud console, request publishing to Google Workspace Marketplace, fill marketplace listing details, and submit for verification. The branding verification typically completes in minutes (claim f4) and then status moves to “Ready to publish” (claim f5).

steps.title: Await Google review and verification
steps.detail: During review, continue using Composio managed auth for existing users and monitor for any reviewer feedback (claim f3).

steps.title: Publish publicly and enable production auth
steps.detail: After approval, switch Composio back to your OAuth client (if not already), enable public availability in Marketplace, and inform users they can now authorize the app at production scale.

whileYouWait.text: Keep existing integrations running using Composio’s managed auth and add test users to validate scopes.

gotchas.text: If your app uses restricted Gmail scopes you must pass an annual security assessment, which can add weeks to the timeline.
